mn57:1.2: On one occasion the Blessed One was living in the Koliyan country. There is a town of the Koliyans called Haliddavasana.
mn57:2.1: Then Puṇṇa, a son of the Koliyans and an ox-duty ascetic, and also Seniya a naked dog-duty ascetic, went to the Blessed One, and Puṇṇa the ox-duty ascetic paid homage to the Blessed One and sat down at one side, while Seniya the naked dog-duty ascetic exchanged greetings with the Blessed One, and when the courteous and amiable talk was finished, he too sat down at one side curled up like a dog.
mn57:2.2: When Puṇṇa the ox-duty ascetic sat down, he asked the Blessed One:
mn57:2.3: ‘Venerable sir, this naked dog-duty ascetic Seniya does what is hard to do: he eats his food when it is thrown on the ground.
mn57:2.4: That dog-duty has long been taken up and practised by him.
mn57:2.5: What will be his destination? What will be his future course?’
mn57:2.6: ‘Enough, Puṇṇa, let that be. Do not ask me that.’
mn57:2.8: A third time Puṇṇa the ox-duty ascetic asked the Blessed One:
mn57:2.9: ‘Venerable sir, this naked dog-duty ascetic Seniya does what is hard to do: he eats his food when it is thrown on the ground.
mn57:2.10: That dog-duty has long been taken up and practised by him.
mn57:2.11: What will be his destination? What will be his future course?’
mn57:2.12: ‘Well, Puṇṇa, since I certainly cannot persuade you when I say
mn57:2.13: “Enough, Puṇṇa, let that be. Do not ask me that”,
mn57:3.1: ‘Here, Puṇṇa, someone develops the dog-duty fully and unstintingly, he develops the dog-habit fully and unstintingly, he develops the dog-mind fully and unstintingly, he develops dog-behaviour fully and unstintingly.
mn57:3.2: Having done that, on that dissolution of the body, after death, he reappears in the company of dogs.
mn57:3.3: But if his view is such as this: “By this virtue or duty or asceticism or life divine I shall become a (great) god or some (lesser) god”, that is wrong view in his case.
mn57:3.4: Now there are two destinations for one with wrong view, I say: hell or the animal womb.
mn57:3.5: So, Puṇṇa, if his dog-duty is perfected it will lead him to the company of dogs; if it is not, it will lead him to hell.’
mn57:4.1: When this was said, Seniya the naked dog-duty ascetic wept and shed tears.
mn57:4.2: Then the Blessed One told Puṇṇa son of the Koliyans and an ox-duty ascetic:
mn57:4.3: ‘Puṇṇa, I could not persuade you when I said
mn57:4.4: “Enough, Puṇṇa, let that be. Do not ask me that”.’
mn57:4.5: ‘Venerable sir, I am not weeping that the Blessed One has spoken thus.
mn57:4.6: Still this dog-duty has long been taken up and practised by me.
mn57:4.7: Venerable sir, there is this Puṇṇa, a son of the Koliyans, and on ox-duty ascetic;
mn57:4.8: that ox-duty has long been taken up and practised by him.
mn57:4.9: What will be his destination. What will be his future course?’
mn57:4.10: ‘Enough, Seniya, let that be. Do not ask me that.’
mn57:4.12: A third time Seniya the naked dog-duty ascetic asked the Blessed One:
mn57:4.13: ‘Venerable sir, there is this Puṇṇa, a son of the Koliyans and an ox-duty;
mn57:4.14: that ox-duty has long been taken up and practised by him.
mn57:4.15: What will be his destination? What will be his future course?’
mn57:4.16: ‘Well, Seniya, since I certainly cannot persuade you when I say:
mn57:4.17: “Enough, Puṇṇa let that be. Do not ask me that”,
mn57:5.1: ‘Here, Seniya, someone develops the ox-duty fully and unstintingly, he develops the ox-habit fully and unstintingly, he develops the ox-mind fully and unstintingly, he develops ox-behaviour fully and unstintingly.
mn57:5.2: Having done that, on the dissolution of the body, after death, he reappears in the company of oxen.
mn57:5.3: But if his view is such as this: “By this virtue or duty or asceticism or life divine I shall become a (great) god or some (lesser) god”, that is wrong view in his case.
mn57:5.4: Now there are two destinations for one with wrong view, I say: hell or the animal womb.
mn57:5.5: So, Seniya, if his ox-duty is perfected, it will lead him to the company of oxen; if it is not, it will lead him to hell.’
mn57:6.1: When this was said, Puṇṇa, a son of the Koliyans and an ox-duty ascetic, wept and shed tears.
mn57:6.2: Then the Blessed One told Seniya, the naked dog-duty ascetic:
mn57:6.3: ‘Seniya, I could not persuade you when I said:
mn57:6.4: “Enough, Seniya, let that be. Do not ask me that”.’
mn57:6.5: ‘Venerable sir, I am not weeping that the Blessed One has spoken thus,
mn57:6.6: still this ox-duty has long been taken up and practised by me.
mn57:6.7: Venerable sir, I have confidence in the Blessed One thus: “The Blessed
mn57:6.8: One is capable of teaching me the Dhamma in such a way that I may abandon this ox-duty and that this naked dog-duty ascetic Seniya may abandon that dog-duty’ ’
mn57:6.9: ‘Then, Puṇṇa, listen and heed well what I shall say.’
mn57:7.1: ‘Puṇṇa, there are four kinds of kamma proclaimed by me after realization myself with direct knowledge.
mn57:7.3: There is dark kamma with dark ripening,
mn57:7.4: there is bright kamma with bright ripening,
mn57:7.5: there is dark-and-bright kamma with dark-and-bright ripening,
mn57:7.6: and there is kamma that is not dark and not bright with neither-dark-nor-bright ripening that conduces to the exhaustion of kamma.
mn57:8.1: ‘What is dark kamma with dark ripening?
mn57:8.2: Here someone produces a (kammic) bodily process (bound up) with affliction, he produces a (kammic) verbal process (bound up) with affliction, he produces a (kammic) mental process (bound up) with affliction.
mn57:8.3: By so doing, he reappears in a world with affliction.
mn57:8.4: When that happens, afflicting contacts touch him.
mn57:8.5: Being touched by these, he feels afflicting feelings entirely painful as in the case of beings in hell.
mn57:8.6: Thus a being’s reappearance is due to a being:
mn57:8.7: he reappears owing to the kammas he has performed.
mn57:8.8: When he has reappeared, contacts touch him.
mn57:8.9: Thus I say are beings heirs of their kammas.
mn57:8.10: This is called dark kamma with dark ripening.
mn57:9.1: ‘And what is bright kamma with bright ripening?
mn57:9.2: Here someone produces a (kammic) bodily process not (bound up) with affliction, he produces a (kammic) verbal process not (bound up) with affliction, he produces a (kammic) mental process not (bound up) with affliction.
mn57:9.3: By so doing, he reappears in a world without affliction.
mn57:9.4: When that happens, unafflicting contacts touch him.
mn57:9.5: Being touched by these, he feels unafflicting feelings entirely pleasant as in the case of the Subhakiṇṇā, the gods of Refulgent Glory.
mn57:9.6: Thus a being’s reappearance is due to a being:
mn57:9.7: he reappears owing to the kammas he has performed.
mn57:9.8: When he has reappeared, contacts touch him.
mn57:9.9: Thus I say are beings heirs of their kammas.
mn57:9.10: This is called bright kamma with bright ripening.
mn57:10.1: What is dark-and-bright kamma with dark-and-bright ripening ?
mn57:10.2: Here someone produces a (kammic) bodily process both (bound up) with affliction and not (bound up) with affliction … verbal process … mental process both (bound up) with affliction and not (bound up) with affliction.
mn57:10.3: By doing so, he reappears in a world both with and without affliction.
mn57:10.4: When that happens, both afflicting and unafflicting contacts touch him.
mn57:10.5: Being touched by these, he feels afflicting and unafflicting feelings with mingled pleasure and pain as in the case of human beings and some gods and some inhabitants of the states of deprivation.
mn57:10.6: Thus a being’s reappearance is due to a being:
mn57:10.7: he reappears owing to the kammas he has performed.
mn57:10.8: When he has reappeared, contacts touch him.
mn57:10.9: Thus I say are beings heirs of their kammas.
mn57:10.10: This is called dark-and-bright kamma with dark-and-bright ripening.
mn57:11.1: ‘What is neither-dark-nor-bright kamma with neither-dark-nor-bright ripening that leads to the exhaustion of kamma?
mn57:11.2: As to these (three kinds of kamma), any volition in abandoning the kind of kamma that is dark with dark ripening, and any volition in abandoning the kind of kamma that is bright with bright ripening, and any volition in abandoning the kind of kamma that is dark-and-bright ripening:
mn57:11.3: this is called neither-dark-nor-bright kamma with neither-dark-nor-bright ripening.
mn57:11.4: ‘These are the four kinds of kamma proclaimed by me after realization myself with direct knowledge.’
mn57:12.1: When this was said, Punna, a son of the Koliyans and an ox-duty ascetic, said to the Blessed One:
mn57:12.3: The Dhamma has been made clear in many ways by Master Gotama as though he were righting the overthrown, revealing the hidden, showing the way to one who is lost, holding up a lamp in the darkness for those with eyesight to see forms.’
mn57:12.4: ‘I go to Master Gotama for refuge and to the Dhamma and to the Sangha. From today let Master Gotama remember me as a follower who has gone to him for refuge for life.’
mn57:13.1: But Seniya the naked dog-duty ascetic, said:
mn57:13.3: The Dhamma has been made clear … for those with eyesight to see forms.’
mn57:13.4: ‘I go to Master Gotama for refuge and to the Dhamma and to the Sangha.
mn57:13.5: I would receive the Going-forth under Master Gotama and the Full Admission.’
mn57:14.1: ‘Seniya, one who belonged formerly to another sect and wants the Going-forth and the Full Admission in this Dhamma and Discipline lives on probation for four months. At the end of the four months bhikkhus who are satisfied in their minds give him the Going-forth into homelessness and also the Full Admission to the bhikkhus’ state.
mn57:14.2: A difference in persons has become known to me in this (probation period).’
mn57:14.3: ‘Venerable sir, if those who belonged formerly to another sect and want the Going-forth and the Full Admission in this Dhamma and Discipline live on probation for four months and at the end of four months bhikkhus who are satisfied in their minds give them the Going-forth into homelessness and the full Admission to the bhikkhus’ state, I will live on probation for four years and at the end of the four years let bhikkhus who are satisfied in their minds give me the Going-forth into homelessness and the Full Admission to the bhikkhus’ state.’
mn57:15.1: Seniya the naked dog-duty ascetic received the Going-forth under the Blessed One, and he received the Full Admission.
mn57:15.2: And not long after his Full Admission, dwelling alone, withdrawn, diligent, ardent, and self-controlled, the venerable Seniya by realization himself with direct knowledge here and now entered upon and abode in that supreme goal of the life divine for the sake of which clansmen rightly go forth from the home life into homelessness.
mn57:15.3: He had direct knowledge thus: ‘Birth is exhausted, the life divine has been lived, what was to be done is done, there is no more of this to come.’
mn57:15.4: And the venerable Seniya became one of the Arahants.
